source.title: QUOTIENT: Two-Party Secure Neural Network Training and Prediction
source.authors: Nitin Agrawal; Ali Shahin Shamsabadi; Matt J. Kusner; A. Gascón

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares a secure adaptive optimizer with SGD on natural-data test-accuracy curves, bearing on V4, but uses a specialized fixed-point training recipe rather than the optimizer comparisons in that version.
record.gate_note: Figure 7 compares QUOTIENT with secure AMSgrad and standard SGD on test-accuracy curves across five datasets. The text says AMSgrad converges faster, especially for convolutional networks; it does not give exact curve values or directly compare training and test error. The accuracy comparisons to floating-point training and WAGE are not rows for the mapped versions.
record.test_reason: The paper evaluates its own secure fixed-point training method. Its optimizer comparison establishes faster convergence, without readable comparative final test accuracies or a limited-tuning generalization comparison. It neither tests nor relies on the finding that adaptive optimizers often generalize worse.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: jointly designing fixed-point training and secure protocols improves accuracy and speed over prior secure-training approaches, and the authors report faster convergence with secure AMSgrad. Accuracy experiments use a non-MPC TensorFlow implementation mirroring the secure computation. The conclusion also acknowledges that convolutional training remains slow and communication-intensive.
record.recipe_differences: Secure two-party training with ternary weights, fixed-point quantization, and a custom AMSgrad variant; compares that setup with standard SGD. The study does not test random-label memorization or measure the training-test gap directly.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that the convergence advantage of secure AMSgrad over secure SGD is especially marked for convolutional networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report faster convergence for their modified fixed-point AMSgrad than secure SGD, especially for convolutional networks. Figure 7 supplies no readable comparative endpoint values and has inconsistent comparator labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A customized adaptive optimizer can accelerate convergence in quantized secure-training recipes.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Computer and Communications Security
record.problems: Figure 7 provides curves without tabulated values or uncertainty estimates; the paper's textual description reports convergence speed rather than comparative held-out accuracy or the training-test gap. The optimizer comparison uses a specialized fixed-point secure-training setup.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted beyond the 60-row limit. Figure 8 compares training variants and floating-point or WAGE baselines, but does not test the mapped claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error beyond the width required for zero training error; neither interpolation nor convergence is established for the reported architecture comparisons.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization under standard gradient training, including local-connectivity controls.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited tuning, training-performance controls, and the effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
An isolated dropout intervention; floating-point comparisons change normalization, loss, output layers and numerical representation as well.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Faster convergence does not establish worse or better final generalization. Figure 8 and Table 3 evaluate the proposed method against training variants and floating-point counterparts; they do not isolate any claim version. The record's displayed quotation exceeds the requested quotation budget and should be shortened or paraphrased.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, and the specified local-connectivity comparisons.
Adam comparisons on image and language benchmarks, limited hyperparameter tuning, training-versus-test performance, and the effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Large-batch training and its generalization gap.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting test accuracy.

relation.reason: The paper discusses generalization and optimizer behavior while evaluating secure-training accuracy and efficiency; it neither tests nor uses the catalog's specific findings.

tranche.reason: These are comparisons of QUOTIENT's own secure-training variants. The stated optimizer result concerns convergence speed, without a controlled result on V4's limited-tuning generalization comparison or another claim version.

source_check.notes: Figure 7's section and caption identify SGD, while its legends identify standard AMSgrad. All five rows are own-method comparisons, linked to no claim version; faster convergence does not establish a generalization advantage.
